caption: Rayleigh scattering, the mechanism
quote: The strong wavelength dependence of the scattering means that shorter (blue) wavelengths are scattered more strongly than longer (red) wavelengths

caption: why the sky is not violet
quote: the scattering of sunlight in the atmosphere is strongly wavelength dependent

user: wait so why isnt it violet then, violet is shorter
agent: Three reasons, from the diffuse sky radiation page: the sun emits less violet than blue, the upper atmosphere absorbs some violet, and our eyes are far less sensitive to violet. The sum reads as blue.

caption: sunset: the same effect over a longer path
quote: the red hues are produced by the scattering of shorter wavelengths out of the line of sight

user: ok so sunsets are red because the blue already got scattered away before it reaches me
agent: Yes. At sunset light crosses roughly 40 times more atmosphere than at noon, so most blue is scattered out of the direct beam before it arrives; what is left is orange and red. Ozone adds a little to the blue at twilight but is not the main cause.
